question: Which of my patients are compensating?
source: the real tool loop: guarded SQL on copilot_ro over the simulated history

answer.answer:
Three patients are compensating over the last 21 days (depth improving while load on the affected leg drops), most first:
1. Maya Ellis (right side): squat depth 61.3° → 85.3°, load on the affected leg 47.9% → 36.8%.
2. Daniel Reyes (left side): squat depth 70° → 82.1°, load on the affected leg 48% → 41.9%.
3. Grace Kim (right side): squat depth 64.9° → 71.9°, load on the affected leg 48.8% → 44.8%.
Maya Ellis's pain after back-to-back training days averaged 6/10, versus 2.3/10 otherwise.
I drafted a plan proposal for you to review: a rest day between squat days and a weight-shift drill.

charts.title: Maya Ellis: squat depth vs load on the affected leg

evidence: progress_v (squat, last 21 days): mean of the first vs last 3 session days of p95_knee and affected_load_pct
sessions.pain_post for Maya Ellis: 6 after a training day (6 days) vs 2.3 (6 days)

sql.query: WITH w AS (SELECT v.patient_id, p.name, p.affected_side, v.day, v.p95_knee, v.affected_load_pct, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY v.patient_id ORDER BY v.day) AS first_n, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY v.patient_id ORDER BY v.day DESC) AS last_n, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY v.patient_id) AS days FROM progress_v AS v JOIN patients AS p ON p.id = v.patient_id WHERE v.exercise_id = 'squat' AND v.affected_load_pct IS NOT NULL AND v.day >= CAST((CURRENT_TIMESTAMP AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago') AS DATE) - 21) SELECT patient_id, name, affected_side, MAX(days) AS days, ROUND(CAST(AVG(p95_knee) FILTER(WHERE first_n <= 3) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS depth_from, ROUND(CAST(AVG(p95_knee) FILTER(WHERE last_n <= 3) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS depth_to, ROUND(CAST(AVG(affected_load_pct) FILTER(WHERE first_n <= 3) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS load_from, ROUND(CAST(AVG(affected_load_pct) FILTER(WHERE last_n <= 3) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS load_to, ROUND(CAST((AVG(affected_load_pct) FILTER(WHERE first_n <= 3) - AVG(affected_load_pct) FILTER(WHERE last_n <= 3)) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS load_drop FROM w WHERE days >= 6 GROUP BY patient_id, name, affected_side HAVING AVG(p95_knee) FILTER(WHERE last_n <= 3) - AVG(p95_knee) FILTER(WHERE first_n <= 3) > 5 AND AVG(affected_load_pct) FILTER(WHERE first_n <= 3) - AVG(affected_load_pct) FILTER(WHERE last_n <= 3) > 2 ORDER BY load_drop DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 200

SELECT CAST(day AS DATE) AS day, ROUND(CAST(p95_knee AS DECIMAL), 1) AS p95_knee, ROUND(CAST(affected_load_pct AS DECIMAL), 1) AS affected_load_pct FROM progress_v WHERE patient_id = 'maya' AND exercise_id = 'squat' AND day >= CAST((CURRENT_TIMESTAMP AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago') AS DATE) - 21 ORDER BY day LIMIT 200

WITH d AS (SELECT CAST((started_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago') AS DATE) AS day, MAX(pain_post) AS pain_post FROM sessions WHERE patient_id = 'maya' AND exercise_id = 'squat' AND started_at >= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL '21 DAYS' GROUP BY 1), t AS (SELECT day, pain_post, COALESCE(day - LAG(day) OVER (ORDER BY day) = 1, FALSE) AS after_training_day FROM d) SELECT after_training_day, COUNT(*) AS days, ROUND(CAST(AVG(pain_post) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS avg_pain_post FROM t GROUP BY after_training_day ORDER BY after_training_day LIMIT 200
